key_insight: MECx accelerates discovery of low-energy ordered alloy configurations by combining Monte Carlo search with a surrogate model trained on bond-count-stratified DFT data.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical exploration of ordering in complex multi-principal element alloys, helping identify microstructures that can improve mechanical and thermodynamic performance.
method: Train surrogate energies on 100 DFT-labeled configurations sampled across bond-count space.
Use the surrogate to guide Monte Carlo exploration of large configurational spaces.
Validate transferred models and predicted orderings against direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and simulated diffraction signatures.
evidence_signal: In ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys, MECx found configurations lower in energy than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits, and the predictions matched direct-search ordering patterns and neutron diffraction signatures.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the compact training set, so sparse or biased bond-space coverage could miss important low-energy states.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
